analysis.title: Americas Consumer Staples: NielsenIQ First Take: Total store sales growth consistent in last L4wk but slower for Food & HPC
key_insights: NielsenIQ data for the week ending October 31, 2026 shows total store sales up +2% in the latest quad-week. Growth was roughly stable in the latest 2 weeks versus the prior 2 weeks.
By department over the latest quad-week, growth was led by Seafood (+7%), Health & Beauty Care (+5%), Household Care (+4%) and Grocery (+3%). Meat (-2%) and Deli (-2%) declined the most.

Food and HPC sales growth both decelerated in the latest quad-week. Food posted marginally greater declines, and HPC growth slowed sequentially from last month. Both improved on a 2-year stacked basis.
HPC sales growth slowed to +3.9% from +4.4% last month. Lower price growth was partly offset by higher volume growth, and sales on promotion rose +30bps y/y.

KVUE led HPC at up mid-single-digit (+MSD) in the latest quad-week, up from low-single-digit (+LSD) last month. Volume growth was stronger and price declines were slightly larger. KVUE continued to lead the latest 2 weeks at +HSD growth.
CHD, CL, CLX and KMB posted solid sales growth acceleration. CHD, CLX and KMB were primarily volume-led. CL was primarily price-led with flattish volume.

PG sales growth was decent but slowed sequentially, driven by slower volume growth and unchanged pricing. Most HPC names decelerated in the latest 2 weeks relative to the prior 2 weeks, with KVUE the notable exception.
Private label dollar share change at the total store level moderated, at -0.2 percentage points y/y in the rolling 4 weeks ending 10/17/26 versus -0.3 points in the two prior periods.

In non-alcoholic beverages, dollar sales growth largely accelerated on a 2-week versus 4-week basis for energy drinks, CSDs, bottled water and sports drinks. It decelerated for sparkling water, RTD tea and coconut water, and was broadly stable for RTD coffee.
By non-alcoholic beverage company, sales growth improved on a four-week basis versus last month for MNST (ex-Bang), PEP, KO and KDP. It worsened for COCO and CELH.

In alcoholic beverages, 2-week versus 4-week trends improved for beer, FMB/cider/seltzers and spirits, and were broadly stable for wine. By company, STZ, TAP and SAM improved versus last month and BF was broadly stable.
In tobacco and nicotine, cigarette dollar sales declines eased to -0.6% over 2 weeks from -1.7% over 4 weeks. MO, IMB and BAT improved versus last month and PM was broadly stable.
Packaged Food sales decelerated to -1.5% in the latest quad-week from -0.9% last month, due to lower prices. MDLZ accelerated on higher volumes.
CAG, HRL, KHC, OFRM, SFD and TSN decelerated on lower volumes in the latest quad-week. HSY and GIS decelerated on lower prices.
On a 12-week basis, sales accelerated for KHC. CAG, GIS, HRL, HSY, MDLZ, OFRM, SFD and TSN decelerated.
risk_factors: Packaged Food price declines and lower volumes at several names (CAG, HRL, KHC, OFRM, SFD, TSN) pressure Food sales growth.
HPC growth on a 2-year stacked basis moderated more significantly than the y/y slowdown, per the report's section header.
Latest 2-week sales growth broadly decelerated for most HPC names versus the prior 2 weeks.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows weekly sales growth by department for weeks ending 10/10 to 10/31/26. Seafood was +7% over the latest 4 weeks, Health & Beauty Care +5%, Meat -2% and Deli -2%, with Total Store at +2%.
Exhibit 6 shows beverage category dollar sales growth over L2wk versus L4wk. Non-Alcoholic Beer was +10.1% versus +10.6%, Coconut Water +18.5% versus +20.5%, and Tea - Liquid -31.2% versus -30.9%.
